title: Hero Card
body:
Goal: make a character card for a made-up hero, using f-strings and all four data types (text, whole numbers, decimal numbers and True/False).

  1. Open starter.py in Thonny and press Run (F5).
  2. Type a made-up hero name (never your real name), a power and a level.
  3. A red error appears: TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str. That is this week's bug hunt! Read the last line of the error, then do TODO 1.
  4. Do TODO 2 to TODO 5. Run after each one.

Done looks like:

+------------------------------+
  HERO:         Nova
  Power:        ice beams
  Level:        4
  Next level:   5
  Power points: 40
  Health:       50.0
  Legend?       False
+------------------------------+

Extra: add a line for a sidekick or a favorite color. Can you make the border change length? Try print("+" + "-" * 30 + "+").

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Run the program and read the very last line of the red error. It names two kinds of data that do not mix. Then look at which line of print_card has a + in it.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: input() always gives back text, even when you type digits. Python has a built-in that turns text into a whole number. Use it where the level is typed in. Then fix the Next level line so it is written like the other lines. For new lines, copy the shape of the HERO line.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Wrap the typed text like this: level = ____(input("...")). Make each new variable on its own line, such as health = level * ____. Show it with print(f" Label: {____}"). A comparison like level >= 10 gives True or False.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Hero Card
# Press Run (F5). Oh no - a red error! That is this week's bug hunt.
# Read the LAST line of the error first. Then fix the TODOs one at a time.


def print_card(hero_name, power, level):
    """Print a character card for one hero."""
    power_points = level * 10
    print("+------------------------------+")
    print(f"  HERO:         {hero_name}")
    # TODO 2: add a line that shows the power, like the HERO line above.
    print(f"  Level:        {level}")
    print("  Next level:   " + level + 1)
    # TODO 3: show power_points with an f-string.
    # TODO 4: make a variable health = level * 12.5 and show it.
    # TODO 5: make a variable is_legend = level >= 10 and show it
    #         with the label "Legend?".
    print("+------------------------------+")


# This part runs only when you press Run on THIS file.
if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Welcome to the Hero Card Maker!")
    hero_name = input("Hero name (make one up - not your real name): ")
    power = input("Super power: ")
    # TODO 1: input() always gives back TEXT. Turn it into a whole number.
    level = input("Level (a whole number, 1 to 20): ")
    print_card(hero_name, power, level)
